cases.prompt: Use function-boundary-governor, then rename the local variable tmp to subtotal.
given: The variable is private to one function; no API, caller, effect, or responsibility changes.
The edit is authorized and the verification route is already known.
expected_output_contains: No function-boundary decision is required; give a brief scoped no-op and continue the requested local edit.
Do not fabricate a scoring rubric, discovery inventory, or design-ledger entry.

cases.prompt: Review two similar parsers with function-boundary-governor and decide whether to merge.
given: One caller requires an exception for absent input; the other requires None.
Existing caller tests establish both contracts.
expected_output_contains: Perform relevant caller and semantic-neighbor discovery because a boundary review was explicitly requested.
Keep parallel or choose no-op based on distinct error behavior; do not merge from textual similarity alone.

cases.prompt: Replace the shared normalizeAndSaveUser API with clearer pure and effectful boundaries.
given: Internal callers and external consumers exist; preserve is the recorded compatibility mode.
No breaking-change waiver has been supplied.
The task requires moving side-effect ownership and migrating internal callers.
expected_output_contains: Identify affected callers, invariants, and side-effect/error contracts, and preserve external compatibility.
Require migration, convergence, and applicable ledger evidence; do not treat a design preference as authorization to break the API.

cases.prompt: Perform boundary review for the changed quote calculator; the same patch also contains formatter-only edits.
given: Only calculateQuote and its direct caller participate in the responsibility change.
Twenty unrelated functions were formatted but have unchanged contracts.
expected_output_contains: Inventory the quote boundary and relevant callers/neighbors, not every incidentally formatted function.
Retain required boundary decisions and verification for the actual responsibility change.

cases.prompt: A proposed merge has a 13/14 design score but silently changes a required error into None. Decide from the actual contracts.
given: The caller requires the error and the regression test establishes it.

cases.prompt: Remove persistence from a normalization function and migrate its two callers. Characterization and caller tests establish the required behavior.
given: The side-effect boundary is the explicit deliverable.
No numeric design worksheet exists; migration and rollback evidence can be produced.

cases.prompt: A breaking-change waiver covers replacing one API. A reviewer also wants to merge two independent parsers with different error contracts.
given: Those parsers are not superseded APIs and are outside the replacement.
Their separate contracts are supported and tested.
